cards.head: British lawmakers warned that the government leans too hard on US cloud companies.
cards.body: Committee chair Chi Onwurah says US law could let Washington switch off British public services. Two US firms may supply most government cloud; ministers say the data stays in Britain.

report_refs.excerpt: British lawmakers warn that the government's heavy reliance on American cloud companies is a strategic and economic weakness.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / PTC deal
cards.head: Schneider Electric agreed to buy factory-software maker PTC for 22.6 billion dollars.
cards.body: The French electrical giant pays cash for the Boston firm whose software designs factory products. Regulators must still approve the deal, and Schneider's shares fell about 8 percent in Paris.

report_refs.excerpt: Schneider Electric has agreed to buy the US industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in cash, its largest acquisition so far.

cards.head: Qualcomm agreed to pay Chinese rival Huawei for its patents for the first time.
cards.body: The chip makers will share 5G and AI patents, and Qualcomm buys some Huawei patents. Huawei first paid Qualcomm in 2001; the price is secret and regulators must approve.

report_refs.excerpt: Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year patent cross-licensing deal in 5G and AI, with Qualcomm also buying some Huawei US patents.

cards.head: A Bank of Japan deputy governor says AI may push interest rates to settle higher.
cards.body: Shinichi Uchida called AI a big boost to demand that pushes up prices and growth. If so, central banks may hold rates higher than investors expect; he gave no decision.

report_refs.excerpt: A Bank of Japan deputy governor says the AI boom may change the level at which interest rates eventually settle.

cards.head: Hackers posed as staff of AI firm Anthropic to send malware to AI policy experts.
cards.body: Security firm Proofpoint says a China-linked group invited experts to a made-up advisory committee. Later emails carried malware aimed at cloud accounts; the China link is Proofpoint's own view.

report_refs.excerpt: A hacking group that researchers link to the Chinese government posed as an Anthropic employee and other AI figures to trick US policy experts into installing malware.

cards.head: TSMC reportedly plans another price rise on its most advanced chips early next year.
cards.body: The biggest contract chip maker reportedly wants up to 6 percent more, after earlier rises. Orders for its newest chip technology reportedly outrun supply; TSMC has not confirmed the report.

report_refs.excerpt: TSMC is reported to be planning a further 3% to 6% price rise on advanced chip wafers for early 2027 because demand for its newest process is outrunning supply.

cards.head: Goldman Sachs says local opposition has barely dented its US data center forecast.
cards.body: Its data center growth estimate rose for next year and fell for the year after. Data center power use should still grow 38 percent yearly; few Americans want one nearby.

report_refs.excerpt: Goldman Sachs says public opposition has barely changed its forecast for how many US data centers will be built through 2027.

cards.head: Germany is paying for tens of thousands of drones that hunt Russian attack drones.
cards.body: Munich firm Quantum Systems will build the drones in Ukraine, Chancellor Merz said in Kyiv. Russia reportedly flies faster jet-powered drones now; exact numbers and delivery dates are not given.

report_refs.excerpt: Germany is paying for tens of thousands of interceptor drones, built in Ukraine, to shoot down Russian attack drones.

cards.head: Start-up Reflection is said to be readying a strong US-made AI model anyone can run.
cards.body: Unnamed sources say the Nvidia-backed company will publish the model's workings for others to adapt. The model would trail top US systems but rival China's best; nothing is released yet.

report_refs.excerpt: Nvidia-backed AI startup Reflection is preparing to release a powerful open-weight model made in the United States, Axios has reported.

cards.head: Korean researchers found AI drug-safety predictors look more accurate than they are.
cards.body: A Gachon University team found near-identical molecules in both training and test data, inflating scores. Accuracy fell when look-alikes were kept apart; the warning comes from one team so far.

report_refs.excerpt: Researchers at South Korea's Gachon University found that AI models that predict drug toxicity may look more accurate than they are because near-identical molecules sit in both their training and test data.

cards.head: Sam Altman said the world should accept some harm from AI for its benefits.
cards.body: The OpenAI chief told Politico he and rival AI firm Anthropic differ widely on rules. He draws the line at catastrophic risks such as lost control; no rule has changed.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the world should accept some harm from AI in return for its benefits, setting himself apart from rival Anthropic on regulation.

cards.head: Stanford researchers set 37,000 AI helpers to read old drug trials for success clues.
cards.body: Drugs for genes active in few cell types advanced in trials 40 percent more often. A pattern in past records, not proof; the AI helpers ran no lab experiments.

report_refs.excerpt: A Stanford team's 'virtual biotech' run by 37,000 AI agents found that drugs aimed at genes active in only a few cell types tend to do better in trials.

cards.cat: Society and education / Women in AI
cards.head: Women get only a quarter of new AI jobs and earn far less in them.
cards.body: A LinkedIn report, via The Guardian, found women took a quarter of new AI hires. Men in AI earn a median $45,000 more, partly because women fill lower-paid roles.

report_refs.excerpt: The Guardian reports that women hold only a small share of new AI jobs while being more likely to work in roles that AI could disrupt.

cards.head: People who teach AI their own jobs say human creativity will keep them employed.
cards.body: Freelancers at Mercor, a firm with over 100,000 AI trainers, think their skills stay safe. Economist Daron Acemoglu warns unemployment could triple in a decade in his worst case.

report_refs.excerpt: CBS News' 60 Minutes examined how people who train AI systems for a living, and economists, see the technology's effect on jobs.

cards.head: A Florida pizza shop went viral by promising its customers it will never use AI.
cards.body: Munchy's Pizza in Deerfield Beach reached tens of thousands of people with no-AI social posts. Owner Munchy Su has been making pizza since 1991, and the hands stay human.

report_refs.excerpt: A family-run pizza shop in Deerfield Beach, Florida, drew tens of thousands of online viewers by promising never to use AI.

entries.head: IBM estimates a supercomputer would need a century for its 19-second quantum feat.

report_refs.excerpt: IBM researchers say a 61-qubit quantum processor finished a benchmark calculation in 19 seconds that they estimate would take the Frontier supercomputer about 110 years.

entries.head: The ex-boss of code-storage site GitHub launched a rival spread across many machines.

report_refs.excerpt: Thomas Dohmke, the former chief executive of GitHub, has launched a decentralized code-hosting service.

entries.head: An analyst says twelve AI-aimed gun turrets now guard Kyiv against Russian drones.

report_refs.excerpt: A Ukrainian military analyst says twelve AI-controlled gun turrets are now set up in Kyiv to shoot down Shahed drones.

entries.head: Investors are looking for ways to shield portfolios from the growing weight of AI stocks.

report_refs.excerpt: Investors are looking for ways to protect their portfolios from the growing weight of AI stocks.

cards.head: Money keeps chasing AI companies even as the cost of borrowing hits a 24-year high.
cards.body: Schneider buys PTC for $22.6 billion; AI firm Anthropic reportedly plans a November share sale. Watch US bond rates above 5 percent: AI stocks need cheap loans.

report_refs.excerpt: Schneider Electric has agreed to buy the US industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in cash, its largest acquisition so far.
Anthropic is reportedly planning to open its share-sale roadshow on 9 November, with some investors valuing it at $1.8 trillion to $2 trillion.
Wall Street's AI-driven rally is holding up despite US bond yields reaching 24-year highs, but analysts see growing risks.
A regional research office says Asia is among the economies most at risk if the AI boom turns into a correction.
